Prompt → model
widgets_values: A feathered young dinosaur (with ruffled brown-and-white plumage, sharp claws, and a spiky crested head) moves alertly through a sun-dappled, dense coniferous forest. Sunbeams filter through the tall tree canopy, casting warm golden rays over the mossy undergrowth and ferns. The dinosaur lifts one clawed foot mid-step, head tilted sharply to scan for prey (or predators), its tail fanning slightly for balance. The air glows with soft mist, and the forest hums with quiet rustles—small plants sway as it passes, and dappled light dances across its textured feathers. The camera captures the dynamic, tense stillness of its movement, emphasizing the lush, ancient wilderness and the creature’s vivid, lifelike details.

nodes.title: Long side in pixels (848 = 480p, the model's size)
Seed (new every run; fixed = same video)
Why the split
widgets_values:
## Why the split

The authors' super-resolution code guides the first steps with the upscaled 480p video and switches that guide off once the noise level drops below 0.7. With 6 steps and shift 2 the noise levels are 1.00, 0.91, 0.80, 0.67, 0.50, 0.29, so steps 1-3 use the guide and steps 4-6 only the prompt. The template does the same for 1080p (8 steps, split 4).

**What to expect:** a second mp4, 1280x832 from a 3:2 picture. On the 24 GB test card the whole run (480p clip, then upscale) took 22 min 34 s instead of 7 min 13 s; each of the 6 upscale steps took about 2 min.

nodes.title: How to use · v1.0.0
widgets_values:
## How to use · v1.0.0

**What it does:** Hunyuan Video 1.5 turns one picture and a prompt into a 5 s video. It uses Tencent's 480p image-to-video model that needs only 8 to 12 steps, as an 8.3 GB fp8 file. Core ComfyUI nodes only.

1. **Your inputs** (green group):
   - **Start picture**: the first frame. Any shape; the video keeps its shape. It holds `example.png` until you load your own.
   - **Prompt**: say what moves and what the camera does ("she turns her head and smiles, the camera stays still"). The picture already shows what things look like.
   - **Long side in pixels**: 848 (480p). The other side follows the picture, rounded to 16 px.
   - **Frames**: 121 = 5 s at 24 fps. Use 4n+1 (61, 81, 121).
   - **Steps**: 12, the authors' pick for this model. 8 is faster.
   - **Seed**: new every run; set it to fixed to keep a video.
2. **Models**: all four loaders must show the files from the Downloads note.
3. **Prompt, picture and size**: the size is worked out from the picture here.
4. **Sampling**: the authors' settings for this model: CFG 1, shift 7, euler, simple.
5. **Save**: press **Run**. The mp4 goes to `output/HunyuanVideo15/`.
6. **Optional: upscale to 720p**: bypassed. Select the group and press Ctrl+B to switch it on; it needs two more files (Downloads note) and saves a second, 720p mp4.

**What to expect:** a 5 s, 848x560 mp4 from a 3:2 picture (the shape follows your picture). On the 24 GB test card: 7 min 13 s per clip, 6 min of it the 12 sampling steps (about 30 s each). An RTX 3060 is slower; not measured.

**Tips from the test runs**
- Say what moves and what the camera does; the picture already shows the rest. A hidden face gets invented (the hat test turned a half-hidden face into a smiling one).
- Tiled decode: tile 512, overlap 64, temporal size 128 (keep it at or above the frame count; a smaller value can leave seams between frame chunks, as reported for this VAE).
- The 720p upscale (group 6) took the clip from 7 min to 22 min 34 s on the test card.

**Tested on:** RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell 24 GB, ComfyUI 0.45.3, run with an 8 GiB VRAM budget (--reserve-vram 15.89): peak 11.4 GiB whole GPU (10.5 GiB ComfyUI) with group 6 off, 12.1 GiB with it on. Not run on a 12 GB card.

nodes.title: Downloads + requirements
widgets_values:
## Downloads + requirements

Click a file name to download it. Put it in the folder shown (inside `ComfyUI/models/`).

| Folder | File (click = download) | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `diffusion_models/` | [hunyuanvideo1.5_480p_i2v_step_distilled_fp8_scaled.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/HunyuanVideo_1.5_repackaged/resolve/main/split_files/diffusion_models/hunyuanvideo1.5_480p_i2v_step_distilled_fp8_scaled.safetensors) | 8.34 GB |
| `text_encoders/` | [qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/HunyuanVideo_1.5_repackaged/resolve/main/split_files/text_encoders/qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled.safetensors) | 9.38 GB |
| `text_encoders/` | [byt5_small_glyphxl_fp16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/HunyuanVideo_1.5_repackaged/resolve/main/split_files/text_encoders/byt5_small_glyphxl_fp16.safetensors) | 0.44 GB |
| `vae/` | [hunyuanvideo15_vae_fp16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/HunyuanVideo_1.5_repackaged/resolve/main/split_files/vae/hunyuanvideo15_vae_fp16.safetensors) | 2.52 GB |
| `clip_vision/` | [sigclip_vision_patch14_384.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/sigclip_vision_384/resolve/main/sigclip_vision_patch14_384.safetensors) | 0.86 GB |

Total: about 21.5 GB.

**Only for group 6 (upscale to 720p):**

| Folder | File (click = download) | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `diffusion_models/` | [hunyuanvideo1.5_720p_sr_distilled_fp8_scaled.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/HunyuanVideo_1.5_repackaged/resolve/main/split_files/diffusion_models/hunyuanvideo1.5_720p_sr_distilled_fp8_scaled.safetensors) | 8.34 GB |
| `latent_upscale_models/` | [hunyuanvideo15_latent_upsampler_720p.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/HunyuanVideo_1.5_repackaged/resolve/main/split_files/latent_upscale_models/hunyuanvideo15_latent_upsampler_720p.safetensors) | 0.09 GB |

**VRAM:** 12 GB is the target, **not verified on a 12 GB card**. On a 24 GB card with ComfyUI limited to an 8 GiB budget the peak was 11.4 GiB (whole GPU, 0.9 GiB of it other programs); with the 720p upscale on, 12.1 GiB. The plain VAE Decode ignored the budget (15.5 GiB), so the graph uses the tiled decode.

**Run on ComfyUI 0.45.3. No custom nodes.** Hunyuan Video 1.5 is in core since PR #10819 (November 2025).

Licence: Tencent Hunyuan Community Licence. It does not cover the EU, the UK or South Korea.
